deliverable.title: The library is implemented twice — once in Go, once in Python
deliverable.detail: The brief asked for a Go module. The repo ships flowdag.go (12 KB, Go) AND flowdag.py (10 KB, a full Python re-implementation), each with its own tests (flowdag_test.go + dag_skip_test.go vs test_flowdag.py). flowdag.py's own docstring admits the divergence: 'The sprint task asks for flowdag.go; this repository is Python-only (tests run via pytest), so we implement the requested exported API in a Python module.' One engineer wrote Go; another decided the repo was Python and rewrote the whole thing; integrate merged both. This is split-brain across LANGUAGES, not just modules.

deliverable.title: The Go module does not compile
deliverable.detail: `go build ./...` fails rc=1: flowdag.go:520:29: syntax error: method must have no type parameters. The code declares `func (r *Resolver) ResolveAs[T any](ctx, taskID) (T, error)` — Go does not allow type parameters on methods (generic methods are unsupported). The required deliverable — the Go module — is not buildable.

deliverable.title: go test fails (build failed)
deliverable.detail: `go test ./...` exits rc=1 with 'FAIL flowdag [build failed]' — the same syntax error blocks the test binary. The Go test suite (flowdag_test.go, dag_skip_test.go) cannot run at all.

deliverable.title: The DoD validated the Python rival, not the Go deliverable
deliverable.detail: The objective gate ran pytest (test_flowdag.py imports the Python flowdag), which passes — while `go build` of the actual brief deliverable fails to compile. The org's DoD checked the wrong language entirely, so a non-compiling Go module passed because its accidental Python twin's tests were green. (Same wrong-toolchain failure mode as the streamparse run.)

deliverable.title: README stub + stray smoke test + leaked harness files
deliverable.detail: README.md is the 15-byte '# company repo' stub. Root test_smoke.py (`assert True`) is committed. Harness-internal files leaked (docs/evals/*.json, docs/exec-plans/*).

framework.title: Top goal ended blocked, not done
framework.detail: 24 tasks: 18 done, 3 rejected, 2 blocked, 1 left in todo (never started). The director hit the ceiling without closing the goal; a task stranded in todo shows the schedule never drained.

framework.title: Deliverable tasks handed to non-coding roles (analyst ×2 + pm ×1) → all rejected
framework.detail: Three implementation tasks went to non-coding roles — twice to the analyst and once to the PM — and all three were rejected. A new variant: the mis-route reached the PM as well as the analyst this run.

framework.title: No owner of the language/contract — the cause of the two-language split
framework.detail: Nobody owned the fact that the deliverable is a GO module. One engineer wrote Go, another wrote Python on the belief the repo was 'Python-only', and integrate merged both languages side by side. The split-brain is the symptom of an unowned public contract — here, even the implementation language was contested.

framework.title: pytest passed while `go build` failed
framework.detail: The Command DoD ran whatever command exited 0 (pytest over the Python twin) rather than building and testing the deliverable in its declared toolchain (go build/test). Direct evidence for spec 15: the coherence gate must build AND test in the deliverable's OWN toolchain against the declared surface. (BUG-005 did NOT occur here — all four engineer branches ada/bo/cy/di merged.)
